answer: An identity must be at least 6 epochs old on the wharf ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Because the age is read from the inlet checkpoint rather than self-declared, the plume audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. Running a farm therefore means funding every alias through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent forfeits once and never again. That is 33 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
